subject: Re: Cobalt Dynamics — supplier portal invite lands but login returns identity error
messages:
From: Avery Price <avery.price@cobaltdyn.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com
Cc: procurement_ops@cobaltdyn.com
Date: Thu, 30 May 2029 14:05:00 +0000
Subject: Supplier portal invite — login returns identity fingerprint mismatch (Coupa)

Hi Jordan,

We accepted the supplier invite this morning but when we try to log in to the Coupa supplier portal we get a 403 with the message 'identity fingerprint mismatch'. The button acceptance flow shows success, then the redirect fails.

Attached a quick screenshot (screenshot-403-fingerprint.png) and a short copy of our SAML trace from our IdP. The user we tried is procurement_ops@cobaltdyn.com.

Can you confirm whether your invite is for the tenant 'cobaltdyn.procure.redwood' or the legacy 'cobaltdyn.coupa'? The invite email references 'redwood-suppliers' as the SP and our IdP is Workday SSO with an entityID that recently changed during our migration.

This is blocking our ability to upload onboarding W-9 and bank details — we'd like to get the account live by EOD.

Thanks,
Avery
Avery Price
Sr. Procurement Manager
Cobalt Dynamics

Attachment: screenshot-403-fingerprint.png
Attachment: saml_trace.txt

From: jordan_blake@redwood.com
To: Avery Price <avery.price@cobaltdyn.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 30 May 2029 14:28:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Supplier portal invite — login returns identity fingerprint mismatch (Coupa)

Hi Avery — thanks for the clear repro and the trace.

Quick summary of what I'm seeing on our side: the invite for Cobalt Dynamics was issued against the new tenant alias (cobaltdyn.procure.redwood). The SP assertion includes a RelayState token we validate against a fingerprint derived from the invite email. If the IdP entityID changed during your migration the fingerprint we calculated at invite time may not match the one presented at login, which would cause the 403 you're seeing.

Immediate asks:
- Can you confirm the current IdP entityID exactly as configured in Workday? (The Value that looks like https://idp.cobaltdyn.com/saml2)
- If possible, try an incognito browser or a different device — we sometimes see stale cookies cause the SP to present the old RelayState.

Internal note to Ben / Lauren: Ben — can you check whether the relaystate normalization released on 2029-05-23 might be rejecting the alternate entityID format from Workday? If so, I want a short rollback/fallback plan we can toggle while we verify the entityID with the vendor.

Avery — I can also resend the invite against the legacy alias (cobaltdyn.coupa) as a short-term workaround if you need immediate PO visibility. Which would you prefer?

-Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Partnerships Manager | Redwood Inference

Forwarded attachments: screenshot-403-fingerprint.png, saml_trace.txt

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 30 May 2029 15:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Supplier portal invite — login returns identity fingerprint mismatch (Coupa)

Jordan,

Thanks — I dug into the gateway logs for the time window in the trace and can confirm the incoming SAML assertion presented an entityID of 'https://idp.cobaltdyn.internal/saml'. Our normalization service supports both legacy and canonical hostnames, but the fingerprint calculation also used the 'NameIDFormat' attribute. We shipped a tightened check on 2029-05-23 that rejects mismatched NameIDFormat + entityID pairs (security-led). That explains the 403.

Short-term options:
1) Toggle an internal feature flag (ALLOW_NS_MISMATCH) for the Cobalt tenant while we validate their IdP. This is low risk for a single tenant and reversible.
2) Resend the invite pinned to the legacy alias (Jordan's suggestion) — this avoids the fingerprint path used by canonical invites.
3) Ask Cobalt to change their IdP entityID to match the value embedded in our invite (requires their IdP admin).

I'm fine with option 1 for an emergency unblock while we get the formal change scheduled. I've created a ticket and linked the trace: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PROC-8421.

Ben Carter
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Jordan / Ben — great, thanks for the quick turnaround.

We validated on our side and confirmed there was an internal aliasing change during the Workday migration: the IdP started emitting https://idp.cobaltdyn.internal/saml instead of the public https://idp.cobaltdyn.com/saml. We flipped the flag you suggested (Ben) and the login succeeded immediately; users can now see the onboarding form and upload W-9.

We're happy to update our IdP to emit the public entityID — we'll schedule that with our identity team next week. For now the ALLOW_NS_MISMATCH toggle is fine.

I'll attach the final SAML trace for your records. Please confirm once you close PROC-8421 and if you need any follow-up evidence for your audit.

Thanks again,
Avery
Sr. Procurement Manager
Cobalt Dynamics
